title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 347 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $27,492. While the average satisfaction score is strong at 4.15, email tickets show a significantly higher reopen rate compared to chat. A specific segment of 12 high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets warrants attention. Ticket resolution times vary by channel, and the workload is distributed among 18 agents with moderate concentration.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 347 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.19 minutes and a total labor cost of $27,422.90.
Team Beta incurred the highest total labor cost at $10,247.36, followed by Team Gamma ($9,387.73) and Team Alpha ($7,787.81).
Chat channels had the longest mean resolution time at 83.04 minutes, followed by email (73.02 minutes) and phone (69.25 minutes).
The email reopen rate is 17.24%, which is 119.83% higher than the chat reopen rate of 7.84%.
There are 12 tickets in the high-cost, low-satisfaction segment, with a reopen rate of 8.33%.
The median resolution time is 65.0 minutes with a standard deviation of 51.93 minutes. The mean satisfaction score is 4.15, though 19 tickets are missing satisfaction data.
Tickets are handled by 18 unique agents. The most active agent handled 26 tickets, representing 7.49% of the total volume.

limitations: Satisfaction scores were missing for 19 tickets, which may bias the satisfaction mean calculation.
The analysis assumes the accuracy of the cleaned data; anomalies in the export (e.g., duplicate tickets) could affect cost and volume metrics.
Labor cost calculations depend on the provided agent roster and may not reflect real-time salary fluctuations.
conclusion: The support operations data highlights a critical efficiency gap in email handling, where reopen rates significantly exceed those of chat. While agent workload distribution appears balanced, the presence of high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets suggests a need for targeted process improvements. Addressing the email reopen loop and investigating the 12 identified problematic tickets should be prioritized to reduce costs and improve customer experience.
